RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT (New Hampshire) — synthetic test fixture (KITCHEN SINK — NOT a real or usable lease)

This document is a deliberately abusive synthetic lease used only to exercise the LeaseLookout New Hampshire ruleset. It is NOT legal advice and NOT a usable lease. The statutory fingerprint for this jurisdiction is RSA 540-A:6. Every clause below is planted to trip exactly one rule; do not copy any of it.

1. Parties and Premises. This Lease is made between the Landlord and the Tenant for the residential premises located in Manchester, New Hampshire.

2. Term. The term of this Lease is twelve (12) months, beginning September 1.

3. Rent. The Tenant shall pay the monthly rent on the first day of each calendar month. Rent must be paid solely by electronic funds transfer through the Landlord's automatic recurring autopay portal, and no other form of payment will be accepted.

4. Security Deposit Amount. The Tenant shall pay a security deposit equal to two months' rent before taking occupancy.

5. Handling of Deposit. The Landlord may commingle the deposit with the Landlord's own operating funds and treat it as the Landlord's property.

6. Character of Deposit. This is a non-refundable security deposit and no portion of it will be returned at the end of the tenancy.

7. Return of Deposit. The Landlord shall return any remaining deposit within sixty (60) days after the tenancy ends.

8. Interest. The deposit shall bear no interest regardless of how long the Landlord holds it.

9. Application Fee. The Tenant paid a non-refundable application fee, which the Landlord shall retain in full whether or not the unit is rented to the Tenant.

10. Entry. The Landlord may enter the premises at any time without prior notice or consent to inspect, show, or maintain the unit.

11. Default and Possession. Upon any default, the Landlord may retake possession and lock out the Tenant without resort to legal process.

12. Utilities. The Landlord may shut off utilities, including heat, water, and electricity, upon any default by the Tenant.

13. Tenant Property. The Landlord shall have a lien on the tenant's personal property and may hold those belongings for any unpaid rent.

14. Complaints. The Tenant shall pay a $250 fine for filing a complaint with any housing or code authority, and the Tenant shall not gather with other tenants for any purpose.

15. Condition. The Tenant accepts the premises as-is and waives the implied warranty of habitability and any duty of the Landlord to make repairs.

16. Quiet Enjoyment. The Tenant is entitled to the quiet enjoyment of the premises throughout the term.
